Do you wake up feeling like you got no sleep at all? That constant daytime tiredness or your bed partner’s reports of loud snoring can be telling of something more than just lack of rest: a sleep-associated breathing disorder, such as Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA). Left untreated, these disorders are a silent danger to your long-term health, directly associated with conditions such as heart disease and stroke.

In quality facilities, such as Silver Touch Hospitals, one of the best lungs hospital in Ahmedabad, we know the seriousness of these symptoms. The most important factor for successful treatment is proper diagnosis, and that begins with knowing when an actual sleep study is actually needed.

Seeing the Red Flags: Why a Consultation is Important

A sleep study, or polysomnography (PSG), is the gold standard test. It is usually ordered when a patient or their family members observe the following ongoing and disturbing symptoms:

  • Loud and Irregular Snoring

Consistently loud snoring that is punctuated by brief silent pauses followed by a violent gasp or snort is the classic symptom of sleep apnea. Such pauses signify that breathing has momentarily ceased.

  • Excessive Daytime Sleepiness (EDS)

This is more than tiredness; it is the extreme desire to sleep at times when you need to be awake, for example, while driving, working, or even watching television. Not getting restorative sleep can have a serious effect on concentration and mood.

  • Unexplained Health Issues

If you have been diagnosed with high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes, or other cardiovascular conditions that are hard to control, your doctor will suspect an underlying sleep disorder. Treating the breathing issue can frequently enhance control of these chronic illnesses.

  • Morning Symptoms

Waking up with a persistent dry mouth, scratchy throat, or headache is a common sign of disrupted nocturnal breathing rhythms.
